title: National Best Practices for Implementing and Sustaining a Cold Case Investigation Unit (NCJ 252016)
publisher: National Institute of Justice, US Department of Justice
excerpt: Guide developed with the NIJ Cold Case Investigation Working Group; 23 recommendations in five categories (needs and scope; design; implementation; operation; support). Recommends operationally separate units with experienced investigators assigned exclusively and ready access to DNA testing; notes database hits often occur long after an investigation is initiated. Chapters cover case selection, modernizing the case, victim-centered and trauma-informed approaches, media, and sustaining units.

title: Cold Case Investigations (topic page)
excerpt: Improved DNA methods can process old, degraded or limited biological evidence; samples that earlier gave inconclusive results may yield usable profiles. NIJ supports agencies with lab access for cold case DNA analysis and follow-up investigation.

title: Expert Panel Issues New Best Practices Guide for Cold Case Investigations
excerpt: Summarises the 23 recommendations in five categories; calls for operationally separate, professionally managed cold case units with experienced investigators assigned exclusively; database hits often occur long after an investigation is initiated.

title: CODIS — Combined DNA Index System (brochure)
excerpt: CODIS began as a pilot software project. Architecture: Local DNA Index System (LDIS), State (SDIS), National (NDIS); DNA profiles originate at LDIS, then flow to SDIS and NDIS.

title: Audit report: CODIS program background
publisher: US Department of Justice, Office of the Inspector General
excerpt: The FBI began the CODIS Program as a pilot project in 1990. NDIS became operational in 1998 and is managed by the FBI as the nation's DNA database containing profiles uploaded by participating states.

title: Audit report: DNA Identification Act background
publisher: US Department of Justice, Office of the Inspector General
excerpt: The DNA Identification Act of 1994 (Public Law 103-322) formalized the FBI's authority to establish a national DNA index for law enforcement purposes.

title: Crime in the United States 2016: Clearances
excerpt: Agencies clear offenses by arrest or by exceptional means. Cleared by exceptional means: elements beyond law enforcement's control prevent arresting and formally charging the offender.

title: Homicide clearance rates and UCR closure criteria
excerpt: An offense is cleared by arrest when at least one person has been arrested, charged with the commission of the offense, and turned over to the court for prosecution.

title: Body-Worn Camera Toolkit: Policy
excerpt: BJA toolkit of resources for agencies developing body-worn camera policies, including public release.

title: DOJ announces interim policy for use of forensic genetic genealogy
excerpt: The interim policy has nine sections, including limitations for the use of genetic association to make arrests and case criteria; forensic genealogy is reserved until other investigative techniques have been exhausted and is used if CODIS does not produce a lead.

title: DOJ Announces Guidelines for the Use of Forensic Genetic Genealogy in Solving Crimes
excerpt: Policy takes effect November 1, 2019. Before FGG is an option, all other available techniques, including a search of CODIS, must be exhausted. The profile is compared against genealogy services; law enforcement then uses traditional investigative and genealogical methods.

title: Regulating Forensic Genetic Genealogy: Balancing Privacy Concerns with the Needs of Law Enforcement
excerpt: DOJ policy applies to DOJ and to agencies where DOJ funding is used. Montana and Maryland were the first to regulate law enforcement use of forensic genealogy. Maryland and the District of Columbia prohibit familial searching due to concerns about disproportionate representation in databases. Privacy concerns are discussed.

title: When should police departments release BWC footage to the public?
excerpt: Given differences in state laws, there is no consistent national policy for the release of body-worn camera footage.
